abstract: this paper presents physical interpretations of the change of basis in heun-type equations (heun's and their confluences and reductions) from solutions decaying at two singular points to floquet solutions. a crucial element in these connection relations is the phase acquired by floquet solutions when transitioning between (ir)regular singularities. we exploit a novel `kink method' to compute the quantum momentum of the solutions as convergent series, explicitly at all orders. consequently, by integrating the floquet solutions term by term, the acquired phase can be explicitly derived as a series as well. given that heun equations and their confluences describe ${\cal n}=2$ supersymmetric yang-mills (sym) theories in the nekrasov-shatashvili (ns) background (corresponding to the quantization of seiberg-witten differentials) as well as black hole perturbation theory, tests and predictions can be established in both domains. specifically, we perform a critical verification matching the acquired phase with the dual gauge period, $a_d$. on the gravity side, our explicit and systematic results agree with standard methods used to analyse the teukolsky or regge-wheeler equations. this procedure provides an effective alternative to instanton and gravity computations. ultimately, it marks the initial steps toward establishing a dictionary between integrability and gravitational quantities.

title: a note on the feynman lectures on gravitation
abstract: following feynman's lectures on gravitation, we consider the theory of the gravitational (massless spin-2) field in flat spacetime and present the third- and fourth-order lagrangian densities for the gravitational field. in particular, we present detailed calculations for the third-order lagrangian density. we point out that the expression for the third-order lagrangian density which feynman provided is not a solution of feynman's condition that the third-order lagrangian density must satisfy. however, feynman's third-order lagrangian density gives the correct perihelion shift.

title: nonaxisymmetric (2+1) black holes with dym boundary conditions
abstract: we present the spectrum of stationary black hole solutions associated with the first nontrivial member of the dym family of boundary conditions. the analysis combines the holonomy conditions provided by the chern-simons formulation of ads$_3$ gravity with the periodic solutions of the stationary dym equation. the resulting spacetimes are characterized by two positive real parameters, two positive integers, and a relative phase, generically describing stationary, nonaxisymmetric black holes.

title: linearized $\mathcal{n}=2$ conformal supergravity in the harmonic approach
abstract: using the harmonic superspace approach, we construct the superconformal harmonic action for $\mathcal{n}=2$ weyl supermultiplet. the fundamental objects of the theory are unconstrained analytic potentials $h^{++α\dotα}, h^{++α+}, h^{++\dotα+}, h^{(+4)}$, which distinguishes our construction among the previously known ones. an important role is played by the ``half-analyticity'' conditions introduced in arxiv:2407.08524 [hep-th]. the structure of the harmonic linearized $\mathcal{n}=2$ weyl action to large extent repeats the structure of the $\mathcal{n}=2$ maxwell action, which suggests a conjecture on the possible structure of the complete nonlinear $\mathcal{n}=2$ weyl theory action in the harmonic superspace. we provide a detailed study of the rigid superconformal properties of the proposed action and prove its invariance in both harmonic and chiral superspaces. first steps are also undertaken towards constructing the nonlinear $\mathcal{n}=2$ weyl action, based on an analogy with $\mathcal{n}=2$ maxwell action just mentioned and a generalization of the concept of half-analyticity to curved harmonic superspace.

title: stability of vacuum and quantum dynamics in anti-de sitter spacetimes
abstract: canonical quantization on scalar and maxwell fields is studied for the stability of vacuum and construction of quantum dynamics in anti-de sitter spacetimes. the $ξrϕ^2$ term in the lagrangian of scalar field with $ξ> 5/48$ (mass term just introduces shift of $ξ$) can cause the spectrum of the self-adjoint hamiltonian with negative value not bounded from below. the degrees of freedom corresponding to the negative values are constrained system and are ambiguous in space direction and in commutation relation. the only other algebra accommodated in 3-dimensional space consistent with locality, the anti-commutation relation, is definite confronting the constrain, and trivialize the negative spectrum to be inactive and absent degrees of freedom. thus only the physical bosons corresponding to the non-negative spectrum span the hilbert space. for the maxwell fields as another constrained system, the gauge invariant canonical energy momentum tensor straightforwardly leads to the gauge invariant non-negative hamiltonian. the 2-dimensional independent dynamical degrees of freedom are quantized in temporal gauge. the energy momentum tensors for both quantized fields are renormalized to be finite at operator level, which guarantee the stable vacuum maximally symmetric and the particle fock states the representation of the ads symmetry so(2,3). adopting weinberg's framework, the new covariant free quantum scalar field is reconstructed in the corresponding mode function space isomorphic to the free boson hilbert space, allowing various local effective interaction terms among fields introduced. the yang-feldman equations relate the free fields and the interacting fields with the green functions determined properly in the mode function space.

title: new approach to the calculation of extreme-mass-ratio inspirals with a spinning secondary
abstract: extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (emris) are among the most promising sources for future space-based gravitational-wave (gw) detectors, such as the laser interferometer space antenna. to fully leverage the scientific potential, the gw templates required for parameter estimation must be modeled with high accuracy for eccentric precessing binary systems with nonzero spins. this work introduces a practical and efficient framework for incorporating the effects of secondary spin in fully generic, eccentric, and off-equatorial emris to the first postadiabatic order. we utilize recently found analytic solutions for the trajectories of spinning bodies in kerr spacetime to significantly simplify the calculation of the corresponding asymptotic gw fluxes. furthermore, thanks to the recently proven flux-balance laws, we show how to express the rates of change of the constants of motion, including the carter-rüdiger constant, using asymptotic teukolsky amplitudes and purely geodesic functions that are already established in the literature. finally, we show how this framework performs in the case of nearly spherical inspirals and numerically demonstrate that the linear-in-spin part of the phases is gauge independent. a wolfram mathematica implementation of the code developed in this work is publicly available in the kerrspinningfluxes package.

title: primordial black hole interpretation of the subsolar merger event s251112cm
abstract: the ligo-virgo-kagra (lvk) candidate event s251112cm suggests that at least one component has a subsolar mass. since such objects cannot be produced through standard stellar evolution, this observation provides a possible indication of nonstandard formation channels. primordial black holes (pbhs), formed from the collapse of primordial density fluctuations in the early universe, are a well-motivated candidate. we investigate the interpretation of s251112cm as the merger of two pbhs in the mass range $0.20$-$1\,m_\odot$, within the parameter space directly covered by the o4a subsolar search. combining analytic estimates of the pbh merger rate with current observational constraints on their abundance and the sensitivity of lvk searches, we compute the probability of observing such an event. we consider both a monochromatic pbh mass function and extended lognormal distributions. within the relaxed constraint scenario, the detection probability can approach unity toward the upper end of the mass range. a lognormal mass distribution of moderate width can enhance the probability relative to the monochromatic case, whereas a broader distribution can instead suppress it. our results show that a pbh interpretation of s251112cm is compatible with current observational bounds even for a subdominant pbh abundance. owing to the dependence of our results on astrophysical uncertainties, such as those affecting the constraints on the abundance of pbhs, they cannot be regarded as conclusive with respect to the nature of the detected event. at the same time, our analysis highlights the potential of subsolar gravitational wave events as a probe of pbhs and their contribution to dark matter.

title: the point-particle-limit effective-source approach for computing gravitational self-force in the lorenz gauge
abstract: the traditional effective-source method is hampered by complex analytical expressions and the inherent smoothness limit, which incur high computational costs and complicate implementation. to overcome these limitations, we introduce the point-particle-limit effective source method, which analytically takes the size of the effective source to zero, thereby transforming the problem into a well-defined jump condition of retarded metric field at the particle position governed by the local singular field. this formulation naturally pairs with a discontinuous galerkin scheme, whose inherent capacity for accommodating solution discontinuities enables highly accurate enforcement of the jump conditions. we apply both the traditional and point-particle-limit effective source method to calculate the time-domain gravitational metric perturbation and gravitational self-force in the lorenz gauge on a point particle in a circular orbit around a schwarzschild black hole. the comparison of numerical results shows the excellent advantage of the point-particle-limit effective source method, which validates the correctness and efficiency of the point-particle-limit effective source method and thereby establishes a numerical foundation for computing generic geodesic orbits or long-time self-consistent orbital evolution.

title: loop integrals in de sitter spacetime: the parity-split ibp system and $\mathrm{d}\log$-form differential equations
abstract: we develop integration-by-parts (ibp) reduction and differential equations for massive loop integrals of cosmological correlators in de sitter (ds) spacetime, demonstrating the feasibility of this approach. we identify a structural property of the ds ibp system: for an $n$-propagator family, it splits into $2^n$ closed subsystems classified by the parity of the propagator indices. we further formulate a baikov representation for loop integrals in ds space and derive the corresponding dimensional recurrence relations. in flat spacetime, intersection theory shows that $\mathrm{d}\log$-form master integrands lead to $\mathrm{d}\log$-form differential equations. motivated by fibration intersection theory, we conjecture that this construction extends to ds integrands involving hankel functions. we verify this conjecture in the one-loop bubble family and determine the associated alphabet.

title: generalized first law and smarr-type relation: beyond additivity and extensivity
abstract: in this work, we develop a general framework for deriving the first law of black hole thermodynamics and the associated smarr-type relation for 4-dimensional static spherically symmetric spacetimes within a broad class of generalized entropy models. in addition, by employing the entropy representation for the reissner--nordström (rn) black hole, we determine a concise curvature functional that depends only on this representation and its derivatives. a general flatness condition is derived, demonstrating that when the entropy hessian metric is regular and nondegenerate, both homogeneous power-law transformations and a separate logarithmic branch leave the rn black hole's ruppeiner geometry flat. on the other hand, rényi, sharma-mittal, kaniadakis, and lqg-inspired entropy deformations typically give rise to nonvanishing curvature in the regular thermodynamic regime, demonstrating that the extremality of the rn black hole does not by itself require a curvature divergence.

title: inpainting to search for premerger massive black hole binaries in realistic lisa datasets
abstract: a key science target of the large interferometer space antenna (lisa) is to carry out multi-messenger observations of massive black hole binaries, observing the merger simultaneously in gravitational waves and with electromagnetic observatories. identifying that a merger is happening and providing an updating estimate of the sky location in the hours, days and weeks before the merger is critical to enable electromagnetic observations of the merger event. in this work we demonstrate and compare two methods for premerger identification of massive black hole binaries; a zero-latency filter approach and, for the first time, an approach using an ``inpainting'' technique. we apply these methods to the lisa data challenge dataset 2a--sangria-hm--and demonstrate the successful recovery of the 14 signals in the dataset that we expected to be identifiable at least half a day before merger. we show that the inpainting method can identify premerger signals even when gaps are present in the data, demonstrating the recovery of a signal even when 3 day-long data gaps are added to the 14 days preceding merger. finally, we explore the challenge of overlapping signals, using a region of overlapping signals in the sangria-hm dataset, all of which merge within a 10-day window, and show how removing signals that have been confidently identified from the data allows us to identify quieter signals in the same period.

title: chaos bound for spinning particles in kerr-newman-ads black holes
abstract: in this paper, we investigate the chaos bound violation of spinning charged test particles in the kerr--newman--ads spacetime by comparing the lyapunov exponent of unstable circular orbits with the black hole surface gravity. we find that the violation is governed by the relative balance between the local orbital-instability and surface gravity scales, while spacetime rotation, charge, ads curvature, and particle spin modify this balance in different ways. in rotating backgrounds, the violation depends strongly on the relative orientation between the particle total angular momentum and the black hole rotation, with anti-aligned configurations generally favoring violation. particle spin further shifts the violation boundary through spin--curvature coupling, although its influence remains comparatively weak over the spin range considered. the cosmological constant has a background-dependent influence. these results show that the parameter dependence of chaos bound violation reflects the competition between the local orbital-instability and surface gravity scales.

title: gravitational wave echoes as probes of the maximum mass of strange stars in quadratic curvature-matter coupled gravity
abstract: gravitational wave astronomy provides a powerful avenue for probing exotic compact stars. recent analyses of gw170817 have reported possible post-merger gravitational wave echoes with a significance of $4.2σ$ and a dominant frequency near $72,\text{hz}$. such echoes may arise from ultracompact remnants possessing photon spheres that partially trap gravitational perturbations. in general relativity, photon-sphere formation requires the stellar compactness to lie between one-third and four-ninths, a condition difficult to achieve with realistic equations of state. here, we investigate this possibility in quadratic curvature gravity with non-minimal matter coupling, considering strange stars described by the mit bag model equation of state. by solving the modified tolman-oppenheimer-volkoff equations, we obtain mass-radius relations and identify configurations capable of supporting photon spheres and gravitational wave echoes. the modified buchdahl limit permits more compact stellar solutions, while photon-sphere constraints restrict the viable parameter space. we find that increasing the bag constant reduces the maximum mass and echo time, shifting the echo frequency toward the khz regime. the echo constraints impose more stringent maximum mass-radius limits than hydrostatic equilibrium, suggesting revised maximum mass bounds for strange stars. we further compute the critical impact parameter and eikonal quasi-normal modes, demonstrating how modified gravity parameters systematically alter the photon-sphere radius and associated observational signatures. these results establish post-merger strange stars as potential gw echo sources and highlight echoes, optical shadows, and qnms as complementary probes of modified gravity for next-generation detectors such as the einstein telescope and cosmic explorer.

title: color-kinematics duality and the double copy in curved spacetimes
abstract: the double copy relates gravitational data to gauge-theory data, most sharply through color-kinematics duality for flat-space scattering amplitudes. this review surveys the extent to which this idea can be formulated beyond asymptotically flat backgrounds. after recalling the flat-space ingredients needed for comparison, we describe curved-space constructions for boundary correlators and scattering observables in ads, ds, and other non-trivial backgrounds. we then review classical and field-level maps, including kerr--schild, weyl, cotton, twistor, and convolutional double copies. a separate part is devoted to self-dual sectors. throughout, we emphasize both the common structures that survive from flat space and the obstructions introduced by curvature.

title: non-minimally coupled weyl connection gravity in the solar system and at the galactic center
abstract: we explore the phenomenological viability of non-minimally coupled weyl connection gravity by confronting its static, spherically symmetric black hole solutions with classical weak-field solar system tests and stellar-orbit observations near sgr a*. in this geometric framework, non-metricity is encoded via a weyl vector field, giving rise to two distinct families of schwarzschild-like vacuum solutions characterized by a free parameter \(ω\) with dimensions of length. we compute the corrections to four classical observables---gravitational redshift, mercury's perihelion advance, light deflection, and radar echo delay---and derive stringent lower bounds on \(ω\) using current observational data. for solution i (purely radial weyl vector), the leading metric corrections scale as \(1/ω\), yielding bounds as strong as \(ω\gtrsim 10^{30}\) m from perihelion precession. for solution ii (time-radial weyl vector), the corrections scale as \(1/ω^2\), resulting in weaker constraints, with \(ω\gtrsim 10^{20}\) m from the same test. this marked difference arises from the distinct behavior of the linear corrections in each solution: while solution i exhibits an unsuppressed linear term \(2r/ω\) that dominates in the solar system regime, solution ii features a linear term suppressed by an additional factor of \(m/ω\), making the quadratic term \(-r^2/4ω^2\) dominant throughout. we then analyze stellar orbits near the galactic center, finding that current observations of the s2 star provide complementary constraints on both solutions. (...)

title: binary ellis-bronnikov wormholes in 3+1 numerical relativity: mergers, fly-bys and gravitational waves
abstract: we present what are, to our knowledge, the first 3d numerical-relativity evolutions of wormhole binaries: pairs of massive ellis-bronnikov drainholes held open by a ghost scalar field. each throat is an unstable fixed point whose e-fold time matches the gonzález-guzmán-sarbach linear rate to within 1.9%. two throats obey a charge-sign rule: like scalar charges repel and opposite charges attract, with a measured attraction-to-repulsion ratio of $1.462\pm0.022$ against the predicted 3/2, so only opposite-signed pairs merge. a head-on collision forms a common mots around both still-open throats, born with about their combined area. the horizon then loses 28% of its area as it swallows the phantom field, and by $t=100$ lies within 1.4% of the schwarzschild radius of the pair's mass, still shrinking. fly-by pairs form no horizon and both mouths inflate, the one nearest capture radiating the most gravitational-wave energy measured. a lone collapsing throat sheds its seeded quadrupole as a burst ringing at the schwarzschild frequency of the black hole it becomes, and every encounter radiates its own burst of gravitational waves and a scalar dipole of comparable energy and negative sign. a throat survives at most a few orbital periods for any plausible perturbation, and the negative-energy dipole would pump rather than drain the orbit, so these binaries have no inspiral.

title: learning schwarzschild geodesic motion with lagrangian neural networks
abstract: lagrangian neural networks (lnns) learn dynamics from trajectory data by parameterizing a scalar lagrangian and deriving accelerations through the euler--lagrange equation, providing a variational inductive bias that improves physical consistency over purely data-driven models. lnns have recently been extended to general relativistic settings, leaving schwarzschild geodesics as an open challenge. training on complex relativistic systems is hindered by the diversity of the dynamics, as well as numerical instabilities and the difficulty of adequately sampling physically relevant, diverse orbital regimes. we introduce two coordinated improvements: a decoupled position--velocity normalization scheme that independently rescales each coordinate and its time derivatives, reweighting acceleration targets to balance contributions across all channels; and an energy-constrained log-uniformly sampled dataset generation strategy informed by the innermost stable circular orbit (isco) structure. with these improvements, our model accurately reproduces perihelion precession and relativistic time dilation, conserves energy and angular momentum to within a few percent even after completing multiple orbits around the central mass and predicts orbital trajectories across eight orbital scenarios in close, medium, and far-field regimes. these results establish that lnns, augmented with physically motivated normalization and sampling, can reliably learn geodesic dynamics in curved spacetime. our work also represents the first successful training of lnns on schwarzschild geodesics and offers a promising direction for data-driven modeling of complex relativistic systems.

title: flip-flop shocks and tori in bondi-hoyle-lyttleton accretion onto rotating kerr-weyl black holes and their quasi-periodic variability
abstract: we present grhd simulations of bondi-hoyle-lyttleton accretion onto a rotating black hole in weyl conformal gravity, described by the kerr-weyl metric. the equatorial flow is evolved for spins a=0.9m and a=0.5m and several weyl coefficients, which enter through an effective curvature parameter k, and is compared with kerr runs sharing the same setup. for the k considered, the horizon, isco and test-particle frequencies differ from kerr by at most ~2%. however, the curvature term grows as kr^2 and acts at the accretion radius r_acc. the flow is controlled by one quantity, eta=|k|r_acc^3/m, the ratio of curvature-induced to newtonian acceleration at r_acc. for eta<~0.03 a stable shock cone forms, indistinguishable from kerr. for eta~0.2-0.3 the anti-de sitter-like term traps shocked gas behind the black hole and drives persistent flip-flop oscillations. for eta>~1.6 the cone is destroyed and an oscillating torus forms. spin modifies only the inner few gravitational radii and does not change the regime. in strongly deviating models the mean accretion rate is 1.7-3 times the kerr value and varies by 20-60% rms, versus 0.1-1% in kerr-like flows. the power spectra show global qpos with fundamentals at 2.9-4.8 hz for a 10 msun black hole, with harmonic ladders whose 3:2 and 2:1 ratios come from one non-sinusoidal oscillation, not resonances. these lie in the low-frequency qpo band and are unrelated to test-particle frequencies (~70-200 hz). they scale as f_0=xi f_k(r_acc), with xi~0.7-1.1 for stable cones and xi~0.23-0.38 for flip-flop and torus regimes. strong oscillations would be detectable within seconds for a bright galactic source. the required |k| exceeds galactic-rotation-curve values by 18-36 orders of magnitude, so a detected shock-driven qpo would measure a local deviation from kerr, and its absence would constrain |k|.

title: on the utility of textbooks in understanding the renaissance of general relativity
abstract: this paper argues for the historical utility of general relativity textbooks written during, or shortly before, the renaissance of general relativity. more so than research papers, textbooks offer a narrative account of the field--one that may differ substantially from the accounts of other authors addressing the same subject. textbooks on general relativity therefore constitute a distinctive form of testimony to the intellectual forces that shaped general relativity, particularly during its reinvention period from 1955 to the mid-1970s. a second pillar of this argument is the observation that nearly all principal investigators at the research centers previously identified by lalli et al.--centers that functioned as intellectual epicenters of the renaissance of general relativity--eventually produced a textbook associated with their own school of thought. to situate this observation within the broader development of the field, the paper presents a concise history of general relativity textbooks from the theory's inception in 1915-16 to the 1980s. this history illustrates one way in which textbooks can serve as sources for reconstructing the intellectual dynamics of the renaissance of general relativity.

title: robustness of exact $su(n)$ einstein-skyrme solutions: black holes, wormholes and cosmologies
abstract: the $su(2)$ skyrme model admits exact solutions when coupled to general relativity in four spacetime dimensions. here, we demonstrate that relevant gravitational configurations, such as black holes, wormholes, and cosmologies, are robust under the extension to $su(n)$ with an arbitrary number of flavors. we show that key physical features, such as the thermodynamic properties, the baryon number of the configurations, and the geometry, are crucially determined by the number of flavors as well as the coupling constants of the theory. in particular: first, we prove that an increase in the matter content favors the local thermal stability of spherically symmetric black holes. second, for cosmological solutions, we demonstrate analytically that as the hadronic matter content increases, the scale factor grows more slowly due to enhanced gravitational attraction, while the expansion rate (measured by the hubble parameter) increases as a consequence of the higher energy density. third, we find that the throat of traversable wormhole solutions can be enlarged by increasing the number of flavors, since the energy density required to keep the throat open does not grow indefinitely but rather saturates at a finite value.

title: the gregory-laflamme instability of five-dimensional black strings in einstein-gauss-bonnet gravity
abstract: we complement and extend our recent study of the non-linear evolution of the gregory-laflamme instability of black strings in einstein-gauss-bonnet gravity in five spacetime dimensions. first, we study time-dependent perturbations of uniform black strings in einstein-gauss-bonnet theory and determine the growth rates as a function of the coupling. we find that for positive gauss-bonnet couplings, the black strings are more unstable than in general relativity in the sense that the growth rates are larger and shorter wavelengths are unstable. in the second part of the paper we show that the hyperbolicity of the equation of motion of einstein-gauss-bonnet theory is determined by an effective metric when the dynamics is restricted to spherical symmetry in the asymptotically flat directions. when the effective field theory becomes strongly coupled, as it happens near the endpoint of the gregory-laflamme instability of the black string, this effective metric becomes degenerate and the cauchy evolution breaks down. applying this criterion to uniform black strings, we find that for any positive gauss-bonnet coupling there is an open set of regular solutions (including the one of minimal thickness) on which the effective metric degenerates in a neighbourhood of the horizon. therefore, we argue that these solutions cannot be attained from weakly coupled initial data by cauchy evolution and the solutions of the linearized equations around them cannot be interpreted as approximations to nearby non-linear evolutions. we provide further evidence for this picture with non-linear simulations of the gregory-laflamme instability. the non-linear simulations terminate through a loss of hyperbolicity of the tricomi or keldysh type, depending on the sign of the gauss-bonnet coupling.

title: relativistic dynamical friction in kerr-schild coordinates
abstract: simulations of the evolution of matter on static metric backgrounds allow us to estimate backreaction effects like dynamical friction at first order in the matter density. previous simulations of dynamical friction have used boosted isotropic and quasi-isotropic kerr coordinates, which simplifies the extraction of the relevant diagnostics but results in a more complicated implementation of the evolution. in particular, the lack of horizon penetrating coordinates means that high resolutions are needed to ensure convergence, and the boosted, spinning black hole metric cannot easily be written in a closed form, making it more costly to evaluate. in this paper we describe how to reformulate the calculation of the diagnostics in the boosted kerr-schild frame for the non-spinning case. we verify that our implementation reproduces previous results quantifying dynamical friction in wave-like dark matter in the appropriate regimes. we discuss the subtleties of transforming diagnostic observables between frames in a 3+1 evolution and develop a general framework for this process.

title: bessel-hagen currents, reducibility charges, and local gravitational energy
abstract: we consider whether the translation noether current of a linearised metric spin-2 theory admits a strictly gauge-invariant local representative. for fierz-pauli and dynamically regular pure curvature-squared theories in four dimensions, we show that no such representative exists under the stated locality, polynomiality and covariance assumptions. a direct enumeration first excludes nonzero symmetric rank-two tensors at the dimension and derivative order of the quadratic action: in the curvature-squared case, the parity-even conservation kernel consists of the identically vanishing lanczos--lovelock combination, while both parity-odd coefficients vanish. homogeneity of the actions in total derivative number then allows projection by field degree and derivative number, extending the exclusion to all finite-order local polynomial representatives with constant coefficients and no explicit coordinate dependence. the translation current nevertheless defines a nonzero conserved-current class. independently, a constant translation is a killing reducibility parameter of the linearised gauge symmetry and determines a nonzero linear surface-charge class, which is distinct from the quadratic energy current. a separate calculation shows why a direct compensator cancellation available in maxwell theory fails for the metric spin-2 field, although this calculation is not needed for the current-class result. maxwell theory, propagating free $p$-forms and yang--mills theory linearised about the trivial vacuum provide comparisons in which translations are not reducibility parameters and strictly gauge-invariant stress tensors exist. gauss--bonnet and pure flat-space $r^2$ gravity lie outside the regular scope of the result, through variational triviality and dynamical degeneracy, respectively.

title: internal translation gauging and local gravitational energy in weyl gauge theory
abstract: we investigate the local gravitational source and charges obtained by introducing translations as an internal stückelberg redundancy in weyl gauge theory. the internal-$t(4)$-invariant dressed coframe identifies the source of the translational potential with the existing coframe variational derivative, without introducing new dynamics. we derive an excitation/source equation and balance law whose structure is independent of the constitutive parameters of the parity-even quadratic torsion family. the gravitational self-current, defined relative to a specified gravitational/matter split and boundary representative, gives a density invariant under the internal gauge factors once its frame index is contracted with the coframe; this invariance neither establishes ordinary conservation nor identifies the density with the external translation noether current. a surface charge follows by contraction with a covariantly constant internal direction, and we separately derive the three-sector noether superpotential of generalized reducibility, with the asymptotic conditions for conservation of its flux. at the teleparallel equivalent of general relativity (tegr) the excitation reduces to the teleparallel superpotential and the covariant coframe--connection pair gives the schwarzschild adm energy; flat cosmology and transverse-traceless waves give further checks. away from tegr, an exact solution of new general relativity gives a charge whose fractional difference from the kepler mass is half the deviation of the post-newtonian spatial-curvature parameter from unity, at the adopted normalisation; independent hamiltonian charge matching remains open. finally, the integrable hamiltonian charge is invariant under covariant lagrangian boundary terms at fixed reference normalisation and presymplectic representative.

title: an exact rotating black hole solution in palatini kalb-ramond gravity
abstract: we construct an exact stationary axisymmetric vacuum configuration in metric affine kalb-ramond gravity with zero cosmological constant. independent variation of the metric, connection, and antisymmetric field yields the complete field equations and the algebraic relation between the physical and auxiliary geometries. a kerr auxiliary metric and a closed corotating vacuum two form of fixed positive norm determine the physical metric. the tensor kernel contains the horizon generator, and the metrics, independent connection, and vacuum field share a smooth extension across the nonextremal physical killing horizon and the rotation axes at finite radius for unequal deformation factors. we obtain an explicit sufficient domain for a causal exterior and an asymptotically locally flat end at fixed nonpolar angles. the physical hamiltonian yields the timelike and null equations, equatorial effective potentials, circular orbit properties, radial stability, and perihelion advance. numerical photon evolution determines the critical curve on an orthonormal observer screen. its size, shape, and centroid depend on $ε=ξ_2b^2/[2(1+ξ_1b^2)]$ at fixed normalized mass scale and spin, with kerr recovered at $ε=0$. geometric observations probe this combination and retain an exact degeneracy between the curvature couplings. a static equatorial comparison with mercury gives a conditional sensitivity of $2.30\times10^{-11}$ for $|2ε|$ under the stated angular convention and mass setting.
